loop.description: The loop's name. One document per loop; `---` separates loops in a group.

every.description: The loop's clock — how often it runs. Free text (`weekly`, `per_question`, `5m`) because cadence is domain-specific; the linter checks presence, not units.

regulates.description: What the loop steers toward a target.

estimates.description: What it believes but cannot see directly.

observes.description: What actually arrives from the world.

parties.description: Who is involved and what it costs them.

never.description: Guardrails that hold regardless of the objective.

ignoring.description: Declared out of scope. Not decoration — this is the revision frontier, the list you revisit when the loop misbehaves for reasons it cannot see.

name.description: The loop's name. One document per loop; `---` separates loops in a group.

target.description: The setpoint, as a readable comparison — `< 400`, `>= 3 sources`, prose is fine.

computed_from.description: Inputs this quantity is derived from.

confidence.description: How firmly the target itself is held, 0–1. Uncertainty about what you WANT, distinct from uncertainty about the world. A target held at 0.7 and one held at 0.99 warrant different revision policies. Candidate finding, per Briefing §7 — accepted here as an OPTIONAL field only, and it does not enter the primitive catalog on this evidence.

from.description: Signals feeding this belief. Each must appear in `observes`.

method.description: How the belief is formed: bayesian, judgement, frequency, model…

calibrated_by.description: What scores this estimator's PAST predictions against what happened. Its absence is the single most common defect found in real loops — three independent authors, none careless.

explains.description: The quantity this belief is a MODEL OF. Conant & Ashby 1970: every good regulator of a system must be a model of that system. Without this the loop is a reflex.

settled_by.description: The observable that would finally decide this — what makes the belief refutable.

idempotency_basis.description: What makes a repeated update safe. Execution is at-least-once on every durable runtime, and a Bayesian update applied twice double-counts into a well-formed but WRONG posterior.

measures.description: The estimand this signal informs. Omit and it is an orphan.

asserted_by.description: A party who REPORTS this rather than a mechanism that measures it. A reported number is a claim by someone with interests, not an observation.

produced_by.description: An act inside this system that manufactures this signal. Load-bearing for groups: a loop whose every input is produced_by something inside it cannot be corrected from outside.

moves.description: The estimand this act drives. Absence means the target is a wish.

delay.description: Lag between acting and seeing the effect.

reversibility.description: THE LOAD-BEARING FIELD. Approval demanded everywhere is ignored; approval demanded where the act cannot be undone is a rule people follow. `costly` means undoable at real cost.

approval.description: Party whose approval gates this act. Must name a party in `parties`.

consumes.description: Finite resources this act draws down.

do.description: Act(s) to take. Must name entries in `acts`.

escalate.description: Party the loop stops and asks. Must name a party in `parties`.

agent.description: An automated actor. Mutually exclusive with `human`.

bears.description: What this party loses when the loop is wrong. `nothing` is a legitimate and revealing answer — an agent that bears nothing and a human who bears everything is the asymmetry that explains overrides looking irrational against the agent's objective.

sees.description: Estimands whose value reaches this party. A party that bears a consequence and sees nothing is accountable and blind — human oversight as compliance theatre.

asymmetry.description: How this party's exposure differs from others'.
